reasons: This file holds type descriptions only, so it cannot fail on its own.
Whether data is checked against these shapes at run time is not shown in the packet.

terms.meaning: a written description of which fields a piece of data may have and what kind of value each holds
a named type description for a group of fields
a field that may be left out of the data

sections.name: ProjectCandidate
sections.title: Shape of one project candidate
sections.what: Describes one project found on a web page: a required name, country, source address, company roles and confidence score, plus optional fields for power, dates, reactor type, designer and status.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape keeps the extractor and the engine in agreement.
sections.watch_out: The units and operator fields are declared, but nothing in the shown extractor or engine sets them, so they will stay empty.

sections.name: SkipReasons
sections.title: Counts of duplicate skips
sections.what: Two counts inside a run's summary: candidates skipped as repeated names, and projects already linked with no new facts.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the run summary explain why nothing new was added.
sections.watch_out: The names skipReasons and skippedReasons differ by one letter and hold different counts, so they are easy to mix up.

sections.name: SkippedReasons
sections.title: Counts of other skip causes
sections.what: Five counts for why a candidate was not added: already linked, low confidence, missing name or country, repeat within the run, or an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains the run result in plain terms.
sections.watch_out: The label noProjectMatch counts candidates with a missing name or country, not failed matches, and duplicateCompany counts repeated names within one run.

sections.name: DiscoveryResult
sections.title: Summary returned by a discovery run
sections.what: The full report from a run: projects added, existing projects changed and which fields changed, the number of company links, and both sets of skip counts.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the caller one complete report to show or log.
sections.watch_out: The links count goes up on every link attempt, even when the link already existed.

summary: Defines the shapes of the data passed between the extractor and the discovery engine: one project candidate and the summary of a run.
purpose: Keeps the extractor and the engine agreeing on field names and types.
why: Likely reason: one agreed shape for candidates and results means both sides read the same fields.
how: There is no logic in this file. It describes the candidate fields, then the skip counts, then the run result, and the other discovery files use these descriptions.
inputs: None. These are descriptions, not functions.
outputs: Type descriptions used while the code is built.
risks: Types are checked when the code is built, not while the app runs, so data scraped from the web is not checked against them.
debug: If a field is missing where a value is expected, compare what the extractor returns with the candidate shape here. If a count looks wrong, check the matching counter in the engine.
